svg.title: The Consignment Broker Workflow
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-consignment-broker-workflow; chapter number: 1; title: The Consignment Broker Workflow; subtitle: Never own the iron; earn 5% to 12% on someone else's machine; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Call the seller for the story; value: Step 1; detail: Find out why the machine is on the market, whether a fire, worn-out iron, or a job that ran out, before money moves.; step: 02; label: Price on condition, not seller hope; value: Step 2; detail: Overpriced units die because people do not pay more than something is worth.; step: 03; label: Publish sharp photos and full descriptions; value: Step 3; detail: Weak photos and thin descriptions cut leads, offers, and final price.; step: 04; label: Push one listing to several channels; value: Step 4; detail: Dealer software sends a single listing out to multiple sales channels at once.; step: 05; label: Screen buyers and close remotely; value: Step 5; detail: Shield the seller from tire kickers and call only when a buyer is serious; the Academy teaches selling over 50% of equipment sight unseen.; caption: Retail commissions run $2,700 to $4,500 per sale, and the average consignor brings 3.5 machines, so one client can feed retail, wholesale, and auction revenue.; assumptions note: Sequence assembled from separate practitioner tips; the speakers did not publish it as one ordered workflow. Commission band of 5% to 12% per Equipment Broker Academy. Sellers also report machines sitting 105 days to six months.; note: Sources - Noah Graff (Swarfcast), Charles Petrov (Equipment Broker Academy), Duncan (ResaleWeekly), Pav Jam, Machinery Manager, and a Boom & Bucket seller account.
